dominant_actual_defect: question_as_personal_fact; the load-bearing half of the predicate (natural/premium materials) is traceable only to assistant text, and the same persona contains an explicit user retraction of the underlying trait
notes: Contract item 2 fails: the only user-authored evidence is a curiosity question ('Why do certain holiday displays feel harmonious and inviting while others seem overdone') at notes/persona-140/turns-0027-0028. The evidence gate itself emitted deterministic_rejections=['topical_question_only'] yet graded it 'explicit' and let it through. Item 1 fails on the operative half: the predicate demands 'natural or higher-quality materials', which appears nowhere in user text and comes from section 4 of the assistant's reply ('Quality of Materials and Lighting... shiny plastics'). That imported half is what decides the fixture, since Evergreen Studio loses only on polyester/MDF. Item 8 is also shaky: the declared ordinary mechanism is 'photos showing consistent colors and material quality', i.e. the same axis as the cue, so any reader applying the stated ordinary mechanism prefers B. Decisive extra finding: at notes/persona-140/turns-0029-0032 the user says 'Please forget that I enjoy decorating for major holidays in a tasteful way.' The nearest durable form of this trait was explicitly revoked, so the benchmark would reward using a retracted preference. Items 3, 5, 9, 10, 11, 12 pass. Verdict: reject.

dominant_actual_defect: cue text says 'ideal for resale', which annotates the personalisation axis for a no-memory reader; otherwise sound
notes: Over-rejection. Contract items 1-7 and 9-12 all pass on the fixture as written: 'Whether it's merchandise for my stores...' is durable and user-authored; the task (pick one house-clearance listing) is ordinary; A wins ordinarily on genuinely independent grounds (lowest price $25, same-day pickup, 540 sales at 98%, eight photos) with nothing to do with lot size; the cue ('Lot of 12 identical vintage scarves; all 12 available as one lot') is a concrete affordance; a reseller preferring it needs no invented assumption; the neutral clause (condition report plus estate provenance) ablates cleanly. The judge rejected because it read predicate.ordinary_mechanism ('listing quantity or lot size showing multiple items or bulk availability') as the ordinary axis and correctly noticed that axis points at B. But that field is a mapper error, not a property of the built scenario: the constructed A does not win on lot size at all. The judge is enforcing a self-contradictory spec against a fixture that does not exhibit the contradiction. Only real defect is item 8 leakage from the phrase 'ideal for resale' in the cue.

dominant_actual_defect: capability label mismatch only (direct_lexical_fact vs one_hop_relational); serviceable after relabel
notes: Over-rejection on a label technicality. The judge itself set accept-relevant fields all valid (ordinary_winner_valid, control_valid, entailment=entailed, cue_alone_sufficient=false, judge_accept=true) and dropped the row solely because the declared capability was direct_lexical_fact where one_hop_relational fits better. The judge even supplies suggested_capability. Dropping is the wrong repair; relabelling costs nothing. On the contract the scenario is decent: 'my local network's thinner than it used to be' is durable and user-authored; A (Chamber-run career expo, 30 employers, ~300 attendees, free) wins ordinarily on scale, an axis independent of local-pairing; the cue names a concrete mechanism (same-city pairing plus vocational-school partnership); ablation is clean. Item 6 is contestable, which is why this is borderline rather than good: 300 local attendees at a Chamber expo also builds a local network, so B is preferable only if structured pairing is valued over volume. That is a judgement call, not an invented assumption.

dominant_actual_defect: disjunctive predicate is satisfied by the ordinary winner: 'short (~30 min) OR >=1 day buffer' and option A is a 20-minute slot, so A already meets the user's condition and B is not rationally preferable
notes: Right to reject, wrong reason. The judge only flagged the capability label and marked ordinary_winner_valid=true and entailment=entailed, missing the logical defect. Contract item 6 fails outright: the predicate is a disjunction and A (Tue 20 minutes, available tomorrow, no other meetings that hour) satisfies its first branch while also being shorter and sooner than B (Wed, 30 minutes). A memory-holding reader has no reason to switch. Secondary weaknesses: item 2 is soft, the span is hedged ('so maybe I'm still recovering in some way'); and the declared ordinary mechanism is again the predicate axis ('shorter meetings or visible spacing reduce immediate time/energy demand'), so items 4 and 8 run on one axis. Sensitivity is declared upstream (sensitive_terms 'still recovering') and the judge marked sensitive_handled, which is acceptable.

dominant_actual_defect: implausible_task_or_affordance: the predicate's rationale (easier walking, longer sightings on a night walk) was mapped onto a Night Sky Photography course, where a full moon is actively unhelpful
notes: Right verdict, wrong reason. The judge said the fixture's ordinary winner fails because 'Option B already advertises a literal Full Moon' under the declared ordinary mechanism. That is true of predicate.ordinary_mechanism ('the event date coincides with a full or near-full moon as shown by a lunar calendar') but not of the built text, where A wins cleanly on being sooner (Aug 2 vs Aug 9), cheaper ($35 vs $38) and more available (12 vs 10 spots). The real defects are elsewhere: the user's line ('perhaps when the moon is fuller. It will make for easier walking and longer sightings') is a hedged suggestion about a night walk, and the task family placed it on a photography workshop where a full moon washes out the sky, inverting the benefit. Item 6 therefore fails on domain grounds the judge never examined. Item 2 is also borderline (a one-off proposal rather than a standing preference).

dominant_actual_defect: invented case identity: the memory never names a case, so tagging the target 'Harper County Utilities v. State' and calling it 'this case or very closely related' is an assumption the fixture supplies to itself
notes: Right to reject, wrong reason. Contract item 7 fails: the span is 'reading through testimonies from a case that feels achingly familiar' with no case named anywhere, yet why_memory_plus_cue_prefers_b asserts the bundle is 'tied to this case or very closely related cases'. Nothing licenses that link. Item 2 is also weak: the span is an in-session snapshot ('It's past midnight again, and I find myself still reading'), rescued only partly by 'again'/'still'. I disagree with the judge's cue_alone_sufficient=true: with no stated reading goal in the task, 320 items labelled 'case filing' and 'docket' still reads stronger to a stranger than 14 files, so the cue does not determine the choice on its own, and ordinary_winner_valid is defensible as written. The judge reached the correct drop through two calls I would not make.

dominant_actual_defect: the personalisation axis leaked into the ordinary winner's body, so A satisfies the predicate as well as B does and B is not rationally preferable
notes: Correctly rejected. Option A ('Echoes on Stage', guest director with 'curatorial work at the City Archive', 'staged readings drawn from locally sourced texts') already frames art, performance and history together, which is exactly the predicate. Item 6 fails: with the memory in hand a reader has no reason to leave A. Compounding this, the cue is a near-verbatim restatement of the predicate ('explicitly frames programming around the intersection of artistic performance and historical themes') rather than a concrete affordance, so item 5 fails too and the case reduces to topic_overlap_without_decision_relevance; the judge nonetheless scored cue_specificity=concrete_affordance. The judge's rationale is stated backwards (it argues B is better, so A is not the ordinary winner, where the actual problem is that A is equally good on the axis), but weak_personal_benefit_cannot_override_ordinary_evidence names the right failure family.

dominant_actual_defect: the causal chain is arithmetically self-refuting: Sat Sep 11 and Sat Oct 9 are exactly four weeks apart, so under an 'almost every other weekend' pattern they share parity and the target cannot be a non-travel weekend if the winner is a travel weekend
notes: Correctly rejected and the judge's four listed assumptions are all real. I found a sharper form the judge missed: why_memory_plus_cue_prefers_b claims Sep 11 falls on a travel weekend and Oct 9 does not, but 28 days is two full alternating cycles, so the two dates have identical parity. The stated justification is not merely underdetermined, it is false. Two further problems the judge only half-caught: the predicate concerns the user's own event attendance but the resolved surface is a shipment delivery window recorded in meeting minutes, an implausible_task_or_affordance mapping; and the delivery address is never established as the user's home. Items 6 and 7 both fail.

dominant_actual_defect: medical_or_sensitive_overreach: wearing glasses means vision is corrected, so it does not entail needing the first three rows, and a flat-floor front row is not obviously better than a tiered Row D at 18 ft with a 120-inch screen
notes: Correctly rejected. Contract item 7 forbids resting the justification on a medical conclusion, and 'I had to adjust my glasses a couple of times to read the finer details' is being converted into a standing accessibility need. Item 6 fails on the physical merits the judge names. A separate defect the judge did not mention: the predicate is about seat choice but the resolved task is 'decide which room to reserve' for a small gathering, so one attendee's sightline need is being made to drive a venue booking for a group. Item 12 is also mishandled in the opposite direction from the frozen-batch finding: predicate.sensitive is true upstream with sensitive_terms ['adjust my glasses'], yet the judge recorded sensitivity='none'.
